scale_002:n1.prompt:
You are helping me research employee benefits options for my company (health insurance, dental, vision, and 401k retirement plan) as the first step in setting up our benefits program. Before starting, ask me for: my company's state/location (benefits and insurance rules vary by state), current headcount and expected growth over the next 12 months, approximate monthly budget per employee for benefits, whether I want a PEO (professional employer organization) or standalone benefits brokers/carriers, and my target enrollment start date.

Once you have these, research and summarize plausible paths, naming actual real-world services and options (e.g., PEOs like Justworks, Gusto, TriNet, Rippling; standalone health insurance carriers or brokers relevant to my state; dental/vision carriers such as Guardian, MetLife, or VSP; 401k providers such as Guideline, Human Interest, or Fidelity). For each category (health, dental, vision, 401k), describe: typical cost ranges for a company my size, minimum participation/headcount requirements, whether a broker or PEO can bundle multiple benefits together, and rough setup timelines. Note any state-specific requirements (e.g., small group health insurance rules, SHOP marketplace eligibility) and highlight tradeoffs between going through a PEO versus setting up each benefit independently.

Present your findings as a structured comparison document (a markdown table or organized sections) covering: benefit type, example providers, estimated cost range, eligibility/minimums, and setup complexity. Include a short recommendation of 1-2 paths that best fit my headcount and budget, with reasoning.

Done means I have a clear, well-organized research summary I can use to decide which benefits path to pursue next. Report back with the full summary, your recommendation, and any open questions or missing information you need from me to proceed to vendor selection and enrollment.

scale_002:n2.prompt:
You are helping me get quotes for company benefits (health, dental, vision, 401k, and other benefits) as part of our benefits setup process. This is an async step: quote requests you submit now will be answered later by carriers or brokers, so you'll need to track submissions and check back rather than expect instant results.

First, ask me for anything you don't already have: our company legal name, headquarters state/city, number of employees, employee ages/locations if relevant, desired benefit types (health, dental, vision, 401k, others), any budget range or plan preferences, and our contact email/phone for broker follow-up.

Then: research reputable options for us to request quotes from — for health/dental/vision, this includes insurance brokers (e.g., local licensed brokers or online brokerages), carrier marketplaces such as your state's SHOP marketplace, and PEO/HR platforms that bundle benefits (e.g., Gusto, Justworks, TriNet). For 401k, research providers like Guideline, Human Interest, or Fidelity's small-business 401k offerings. For each, note their quote-request process, required information, and typical turnaround time.

Where a provider offers a self-serve online quote-request form, fill it out with our details and submit it. Where quotes require a broker/sales conversation, prepare a summary email or intake form with our company details ready to send, but do not send outreach that commits us or negotiates terms — stop for human sign-off before any broker engagement that isn't a simple form submission.

Report back with: a list of providers contacted, which quotes were submitted directly vs. which need my sign-off to send, expected response timelines, and a simple tracker (provider, benefit type, status, next check-in date) so we can follow up as responses come in.

scale_002:n3.prompt:
You are helping me prepare a benefits plan comparison and negotiation package for our company (health, dental, vision, and 401k). I have fiduciary authority over this spend, so you must prepare everything but stop short of selecting plans or committing to any rates.

First, ask me for anything you need that isn't already available: our company size/headcount, employee census (ages, dependents if known), state(s) of operation, current budget target per employee/month, any broker or carrier portals we already have accounts with, and preferred insurance carriers or a PEO if we have one in mind.

Then do the following:
1. Using our configured credentials, log into any broker/carrier/PEO portals we already have access to and pull current quotes or renewal options for health, dental, vision, and 401k plans.
2. If no portal access exists, research publicly available plan information and typical rate ranges for our company size and location from major carriers (e.g., health insurers, dental/vision providers, 401k plan administrators) to build a comparison baseline.
3. Build a clear side-by-side comparison table: carrier/plan name, coverage tier, monthly premium per employee, deductible/out-of-pocket max, employer vs employee cost split, and any notable exclusions or waiting periods. Do the same for 401k providers (fees, match structure options, fund lineup quality).
4. Draft a one-page recommendation memo highlighting 2-3 top options per category with pros/cons and estimated total monthly/annual cost to the company.
5. Draft any negotiation talking points or questions to raise with brokers/carriers (e.g., volume discounts, multi-year rate locks) for my review.

Do not select a plan, accept a quote, sign up, or commit to any rate — this decision requires my explicit approval. Package the comparison table, memo, and talking points together and report back, then stop for human sign-off.

scale_002:n4.prompt:
You are helping me configure benefits in {{vendor}} (our payroll platform) so employees can enroll in health insurance, dental, vision, and a 401(k)/retirement plan, with deductions and contributions synced to payroll. A human must explicitly approve before any changes are applied — you may prepare everything but must not finalize or submit the setup.

First, ask me for anything you need that isn't already available: our {{vendor}} account access confirmation (use your configured credentials), our company legal name/EIN if required by the benefits module, the specific insurance carriers or plans we've selected (medical, dental, vision) and their plan documents or group numbers, our chosen 401(k) provider details and match/vesting policy, and our target benefits effective date.

Then, using {{vendor}}'s benefits administration area:
1. Navigate to the benefits setup section and begin adding each benefit type (health, dental, vision, 401k).
2. Enter plan details, carrier information, and eligibility rules as provided.
3. Configure payroll deduction and contribution rules so they will sync automatically once approved.
4. Prepare employee enrollment settings (open enrollment window, eligible employee list) but do not send invitations yet.
5. Compile a draft summary showing each benefit plan configured, deduction amounts, employer contribution/match rules, and effective dates.

Do not click any final "confirm," "activate," "approve," or "submit" action inside {{vendor}} — leave the configuration in draft/pending state and stop for human sign-off.

Report back with: a checklist of all benefits configured and their current status (draft/pending), the draft summary of deductions/contributions, any missing information or plan details you still need from me, and a clear note confirming that final activation requires my explicit approval.

scale_002:n5.prompt:
You are helping me announce open enrollment for our new benefits package (health insurance, dental, vision, 401k) using {{vendor}}, our payroll/benefits platform. If you don't already have them, ask me for: our company domain, the list of eligible employees or the employee group/roster location in {{vendor}}, the benefits plan names and effective/enrollment dates, and any specific talking points I want included (e.g., cost-sharing, deadlines, contact person for questions).

Using that information, please:
1. Confirm in {{vendor}} that the health insurance, dental, vision, and 401(k) plans are correctly configured with enrollment and deduction sync to payroll, and note any plans that appear incomplete or misconfigured.
2. Draft a clear team-wide announcement (email or message) explaining the new benefits, enrollment window dates, how to enroll (via {{vendor}}'s employee self-service), and who to contact with questions.
3. Prepare the open enrollment period settings in {{vendor}} (start/end dates, eligible employee group) as a pre-filled draft, without activating it.
4. Compile a short checklist summarizing: plans configured, announcement draft, enrollment window settings, and any outstanding data gaps (e.g., missing employee elections or plan details).

Do not send the announcement, open the enrollment period, or apply any changes in {{vendor}} yourself — this requires my explicit approval. Once your checklist and drafts are ready, stop for human sign-off and present everything to me for review: the announcement text, the enrollment window configuration, and any flagged issues, so I can approve before anything goes live.

scale_002:n6.prompt:
You are helping me monitor the employee benefits enrollment step in {{vendor}} (our payroll platform), where each employee must individually complete their own health insurance, dental, vision, and 401(k) elections through their self-service portal. Employees making these personal elections remains a human step and cannot be completed or influenced by you.

Before starting, ask me for: (1) our {{vendor}} account access confirmation (I will use my configured credentials), and (2) the list of employees expected to enroll (or confirm you should pull this from {{vendor}}'s admin dashboard).

Your tasks:
1. Log into {{vendor}} using my configured credentials and navigate to the benefits administration or enrollment tracking section.
2. Pull a status report showing, for each employee: whether they've been sent their enrollment invitation, whether they've started or completed health/dental/vision elections, and whether they've completed 401(k) enrollment.
3. Identify any employees who have not yet started or who appear stalled partway through (e.g., started but haven't submitted).
4. For employees not yet invited, prepare draft reminder notifications (via {{vendor}}'s messaging feature if available, or draft email text) — but do not send these yourself; stop for human sign-off before any communication goes out.
5. Note the enrollment deadline if one is configured in {{vendor}}, and flag how many days remain.

Since this is an async, third-party-dependent process, treat this as a polling task: run this check now, and note that I should re-run it periodically (e.g., every few days) until all employees show completed status for health insurance, dental, vision, and 401(k) elections.

Report back with: a summary table of enrollment status per employee/benefit type, a list of stalled or unstarted enrollments, drafted reminder messages awaiting my approval, and the deadline countdown. Do not send reminders or make elections on anyone's behalf — stop for human sign-off before any outbound communication.
